deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'tame topology' (topologie modérée). A moderate structure on a set is given by families M_n of 'moderate' subsets of X^n, with axioms M1–M5; M5 requires stability under finite unions. Ens_{M_n} is the category of moderate spaces, and E seems to be the full subcategory of spaces embeddable moderately into some R^A (A finite), R being the reals with their moderate structure.

The previous page asks whether pushouts X1 <- Z -> X2 exist in Ens_{M_n}. This page gives a criterion. The pushout exists in E, and the forgetful functor X ↦ |X| commutes with it (so the underlying set is the set-theoretic gluing X1 ⊔_Z X2), if and only if there is a finite family of (implicitly moderate) functions f_α: X1 -> R and g_α: X2 -> R, α ∈ A, such that:
(a) f_α∘i1 = g_α∘i2 on Z for all α, so the f_α and g_α glue to a map F: X1 ⊔_Z X2 -> R^A;
(b) (f_α): X1 -> R^A and (g_α): X2 -> R^A are injective, i.e. moderate embeddings;
(c) for x1 ∈ X1 \ i1(Z) and x2 ∈ X2 \ i2(Z) there is an α with f_α(x1) ≠ g_α(x2).

Conditions (a)–(c) say exactly that F is well defined and injective. Points of i1(Z) are separated from X2 \ i2(Z) automatically by (b). The image F(X1 ⊔_Z X2) = F(X1) ∪ G(X2) is a finite union of moderate subsets of R^A, hence moderate by M5. The universal property then follows from the proposition on the previous page: a map out of a finite union of moderate parts is moderate iff its restrictions are. The next page proves this via graphs, Γ_f being the finite union of the images of the Γ_{f_i}. The 'only if' direction is trivial: take the coordinate functions of an embedding of the pushout into some R^A.

NB: the same criterion holds for a finite inductive system (X_i) whose images cover a set X. The moderate quotient structure on X exists iff there is a finite family of compatible systems (f_{αi}: X_i -> R moderate)_i descending to functions f_α: X -> R that together give an injection X ↪ R^A.

In modern terms, this is a criterion for a finite gluing of definable sets to be an 'affine' definable set, i.e. embeddable in some R^n. Its purpose is to establish finite colimits and quotients, needed for the corollary on the next page: X/R_f ≅ f(X).
errors: Index inconsistency: 'X1 -> R^I' should read R^A; the family is indexed by A throughout.
The f_α and g_α must be moderate maps; the page does not say so, though it is clearly intended (the NB adds 'modérée').

Tacit hypothesis: i1 and i2 are injective, i.e. moderate embeddings. Otherwise the set-theoretic pushout is a quotient by the equivalence relation generated on Z, and conditions (b) and (a) become restrictive or inconsistent. With (a) and (b) as stated, i1(z)=i1(z') forces i2(z)=i2(z').

In a setting with definable choice or elimination of imaginaries (o-minimal expansions of fields), such pushouts of plain definable sets always exist. The criterion only has content in Grothendieck's more general axiomatic framework, or when topology or properness is also required. The page does not discuss this.

ideas.what: Criterion for existence of a pushout/gluing of moderate (tame) spaces: existence of finitely many compatible moderate real functions giving a joint injective embedding of the glued set into R^A
ideas.modern_name: Affineness of definable/semialgebraic spaces obtained by finite gluing (definable spaces embeddable in R^n)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Robson (embedding semialgebraic spaces, 1983); Delfs–Knebusch (semialgebraic/locally semialgebraic spaces, 1980s); van den Dries, Tame Topology and o-minimal structures (1998), ch. 10
ideas.where_published: Only the programme for 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5–6), without such details

ideas.what: Generalization: the moderate quotient structure on a finite colimit of moderate spaces exists iff compatible systems of moderate functions give an embedding into R^A
ideas.modern_name: Finite colimits / quotients in categories of definable sets; definable quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (definable quotients, ch. 10); elimination of imaginaries in o-minimal theories (Pillay, Steinhorn et al.)

ideas.what: Axiomatic category Ens_{M_n} of sets with families of 'moderate' subsets of powers, studied via existence of colimits and compatibility with the forgetful functor
ideas.modern_name: Structures in the sense of o-minimality / van den Dries's axiomatic tame topology
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the desideratum, not this axiomatization

missed.claim: Grothendieck, around the mid-1970s, framed tame topology categorically. He works with a category of sets carrying families M_n of moderate subsets of the powers X^n. He asks for the existence of finite colimits commuting with the forgetful functor, and reduces this to embeddability in R^A via finitely many real-valued moderate functions. This is close to the later 'definable spaces are affine iff …' theme, developed independently by Robson, Delfs–Knebusch and van den Dries.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents that Grothendieck's unpublished topologie modérée anticipated, at the level of definitions and simple criteria, the categorical treatment of definable sets and definable gluing. The mathematics itself is elementary and contained in later o-minimal literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The criterion is essentially tautological: the gluing embeds iff there are coordinates realizing an injective glued map. Analogous statements are standard in semialgebraic and o-minimal geometry. The interest is mainly historical, showing an early axiomatic and categorical tame-topology framework.
